Prediction data for predictRisk(), keeping patients without measurements

Source: R/dynamicPredictionShared.R
prepare_risk_data.Rd

Without any biomarker measurement up to prediction_time, the longitudinal factor \(f(Y \mid T)\) of the backward joint model is 1, and the predicted risk is that of the survival sub-model alone given the patient's covariates. predictRisk() predicts such patients that way instead of refusing them. This runs the usual drop_after_prediction_time(), align_ordinal_levels() and drop_missing_longitudinal(), then puts back one row per patient left without any measurement: their earliest row, with the biomarker set to NA and time_variable set to their last visit up to prediction_time (min(0, prediction_time) if there is none), which an interval-censored fit takes as the last time they were known to be event-free. The covariates come from that row: the survival sub-model's covariates are baseline values, one row per patient. A warning names these patients. split_no_measurement() separates them again; running this on its own output returns the same data, as "auto" bandcount tuning does.

A patient with measurements of some biomarkers but not of others is still reported as unpredictable, as before.

Usage

prepare_risk_data(
  data_predict_all,
  long_fit_all,
  survival_fit_all,
  prediction_time,
  time_variable,
  survival_variable_all
)

Value

data_predict_all, filtered, with the added rows in the position of each patient's earliest row.
